body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A second Fix all call clears the cancel handle of the run that is already waiting**

The handler sets `reconcileWait = wait` (line 163) before it knows whether this call will get into maintenance mode. Suppose a second `library:reconcile-fix` arrives while the first run is still waiting for the vault to go idle, from another window or a double trigger (the reconcile store guards only within one renderer). `enterMaintenance` rejects it straight away with `MaintenanceAlreadyRunningError` (vault-activity.ts:136-137). Its `finally` then finds `reconcileWait === wait`, because this call overwrote it, and sets it to `null` (line 173). After that, `library:reconcile-cancel` (line 177) has no controller to abort. The first run's dialog shows "waiting" but can no longer be cancelled, and it keeps waiting until the vault goes idle or a recording or export starts.

Fix: only claim the slot when it is free, e.g. `if (reconcileWait) return { status: "already-running" }` before creating the controller. Another option is to keep the previous controller and abort through a set of controllers.

🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A source whose removal check fails is neither removed nor set aside in "set-aside" mode**

`removeSource` returns `"unknown"` when `lstat` of the placed source fails (line 302–305). With `stuck: "rollback"` that case throws (line 277). With `stuck: "set-aside"`, the mode used for staging files, nothing happens: `setAside` runs only from the `catch` at line 269, and line 286 only syncs on `"removed"`. So the bytes end up at `to`, and the staging source keeps a name the stranded sweep still matches. The doc comment of `StuckSource` says such a source is set aside "or marked placed" so it is not swept up as a second recording. If the read error goes away later (a network share comes back, for example), the next sweep can recover the same take a second time. Consider calling `setAside(from, sourceId, to, placed.size)` for `"unknown"` when `stuck !== "rollback"`. Even if the rename fails, it falls back to the marker.

🟡📝 **Consider · docs: onWaiting fires on every release, not only when the set of kinds changes**

The comment says `onWaiting` gets the kinds still in flight "each time that set changes while waiting". But `settle()` (line 178-180) calls `entering.onWaiting?.(this.active())` on every release while `count > 0`. Example: two `library` leases are held and one is released. The set is still `["library"]`, and the callback fires anyway. Either fix the comment ("each time a lease is released while waiting") or keep the last reported set and skip the call when it hasn't changed. Skipping would avoid sending the renderer progress events that repeat the same set.

🟠🧪 **Fix · tests: Screenshot overwrite test accepts any Error, so it doesn't prove the item was found and then refused**

The comment on line 105 says "the item is found and still refused", but the test only checks `toBeInstanceOf(Error)`. `overwriteImage` (library-vault.ts:1196-1199) also throws a plain `Error` when `expectedAssetId` is missing, and an `ItemGoneError` when `resolveIdentity` doesn't match the identity. If identity resolution broke for this sidecar (valid `assetId`, invalid `title`), the test would still pass because of the `ItemGoneError`, even though the refusal path never ran. Assert `toBeInstanceOf(UnreadableRecordError)` instead, as the test above does at line 95. You could also check that the message contains `UNREADABLE_RECORD_MARKER`.

🟠🧪 **Fix · tests: EACCES case isn't skipped when running as root or on Windows**

The `unreadable (EACCES)` case relies on `chmod(manifestPath, 0o000)` to make the manifest unreadable. When the tests run as root (common in CI containers), or on Windows, the file stays readable. The test then reads it as a valid pending manifest (`pendingManifest()`), so the scan never reports `unreadable-orphan-run` and the assertion at line 395 fails.

Other tests that use chmod in this PR guard against this: `vault-reconcile.scan.test.ts:10`, `library-vault.unreadable.test.ts:8` and `library-vault.rename.test.ts:113` each define `const canChmod = process.platform !== "win32" && process.getuid?.() !== 0;`, and `library-vault.test.ts:405` uses `it.skipIf(...)`. This case should be skipped the same way.

There is another option, because this file already mocks `node:fs/promises`: inject the error with `faults.fail = (op, p) => op === "readFile" && p === manifestPath`, changing the injected code to EACCES. That would make the case independent of the platform.

🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Fixture comment says a 6-item chain, but the loop builds 5**

The comment reads "A 6-item chain: titles B…F over files A…E, F free", but the loop at line 97 only creates the five items A–E, and their titles are B–F. Also, the comment sits above the X/Y cycle entries instead of above the loop that builds the chain. Change it to "5-item chain" and move it to line 97 so it matches the fixture.

🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Header comment points to review history instead of what the test covers**

"Fifth review of NIW2-561:" ties the file to a review round that readers can't look up from the code, and it stops meaning anything once the PR merges. The rest of the sentence already lists the three scenarios. Dropping the prefix would match the headers of the sibling files (`no-hard-link`, `move-failure`).

🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Test title doesn't parse**

"a reload %s finalize reserves its destination waits for it" puts two verbs back to back, so it's hard to tell when the reload happens. Something like "a reload %s finalize reserves its destination: the vault stays busy until finalize settles and nothing is overwritten" would say it clearly in the failure output.

🟡📝 **Consider · docs: autosaveEdits' JSDoc now sits on the maintenance-retry effect**

The new `persistRef` / `onLibraryMaintenanceEnded` block (lines 463–474) was inserted between the JSDoc at lines 457–462 ("Write the current edits over the vault item, quietly…") and `autosaveEdits` at line 476, which that JSDoc describes. Editors and tooling now attach that doc to `persistRef` instead. Moving the new block above the JSDoc (for example, right after the `persist` definition) puts the comment back next to the function it describes.

🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: English plural for reconcileKept mixes "their" and "its"**

The `other` branch says "# items kept their names for now (open in the editor, locked by another app, or its new name just taken)". With a plural subject this should be "their new name just taken" (or "their new names"), not "its". The `one` branch is correct as written. The Spanish string already agrees in both branches.

Fixed in 3f1e2b16. The handler now returns `{ status: "already-running" }` when a run already holds the slot, before creating a controller, so the waiting run keeps its cancel handle. Test: `library-ipc.maintenance.test.ts` holds a lease, starts Fix all, calls it again (already-running), then cancels the first (cancelled). It timed out on the old handler.

Fixed in 3f1e2b16. In staging mode an `unknown` source removal now calls `setAside` (rename aside, marker as fallback), so the sweep cannot recover the take twice. Rollback mode is unchanged. New test "staging mode: a source that cannot be checked after placing is set aside" fails without the change.
Fixed the comment in 3f1e2b16: it fires each time a lease is released while waiting, and the set may repeat. I kept the behaviour; the renderer only displays the latest set.
Fixed in 3f1e2b16: the test asserts `UnreadableRecordError` and that the message contains `UNREADABLE_RECORD_MARKER`.
Fixed in 3f1e2b16 with the same `canChmod` guard the other suites use: the EACCES case is filtered out when running as root or on Windows. The corrupt-JSON and bad-schema cases always run.
Fixed in 3f1e2b16: the comment says a 5-item chain and sits above the loop that builds it.
Fixed in 3f1e2b16: dropped the review-round prefix.
Fixed in 3f1e2b16: "a reload %s finalize reserves its destination: the vault stays busy until finalize settles, and nothing is overwritten".
Fixed in 3f1e2b16: the maintenance-retry block moved above the JSDoc, which sits on `autosaveEdits` again.
Fixed in 3f1e2b16: the plural branch says "their new name just taken".
